components.name: Primary Button

components.css: .ds-btn-primary { background: #1a2332; color: #ffffff; font-family: 'DM Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.95rem; padding: 12px 28px; border: none; border-radius: 6px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 220ms ease, transform 220ms cubic-bezier(0.2,0.9,0.4,1.05), box-shadow 220ms ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: #2d3a4a; transform: translateY(-2px); box-shadow: 0 14px 24px -14px rgba(0,0,0,0.22); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #c4913c; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: inline-block; background: transparent; color: #4a5e75; font-family: 'DM Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 500; font-size: 0.875rem; text-decoration: none; padding: 8px 16px; border: 1px solid rgba(74,94,117,0.3); border-radius: 4px; transition: color 220ms ease, border-color 220ms ease; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { color: #c4913c; border-color: #c4913c; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #c4913c; outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview: The personal site of an engineering educator and program builder, read like a well-edited publication run by someone who actually builds things. Magazine-grade editorial rigor (serif display, generous measure, deliberate hierarchy) meets engineering precision (a disciplined navy/steel structure, exact spacing, one accent used on purpose). Gold is the single distinguishing mark, the brushed-brass accent that signals care without raising its voice. The system earns the trust of a skeptical, time-pressed reader by leading with proof: named programs, real numbers, things that were built. Boldness comes from committed typography, confident components, and considered depth, never from decoration.
keyCharacteristics: Editorial serif display over a clean geometric sans body
Navy/steel authority structure with a single gold accent
Tactile, confident components on quiet resting elevation
Proof-forward layout: evidence leads, decoration never does
Light and dark modes, both first-class

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Gold appears on no more than ~10% of any screen. It is the only saturated color in the system; if a second accent feels necessary, the layout is wrong, not the palette.

rules.name: The Gold-on-Light Caution
rules.body: Brushed Gold (#c4913c) is a mid-tone. Never set it as body text on cloud or white; it fails 4.5:1. Use it for marks, borders, and large/bold accents, or darken toward #9a6f28.

rules.name: The Serif-Authority Rule
rules.body: Every heading is serif; every functional string (labels, nav, metadata, buttons) is sans. The split is the system's voice; do not mix it.

rules.name: The One Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: The gold uppercase label is a real device, not scaffolding. Use it where it carries information; do not stamp it above every section.

rules.name: The Quiet-Depth Rule
rules.body: Resting elevation is whisper-low; the drama lives in the change on hover, not the resting state. If a resting shadow is visible from across the room, it is too heavy.

dos: Do lead every section with proof (named programs, real numbers, built outcomes); let evidence carry the page.
Do keep gold to ~10% of any screen, as marks, borders, and accents only.
Do use serif for all headings and DM Sans for all working text; hold the split.
Do keep body measure at 65-75ch and body contrast at 4.5:1 (push toward 7:1 / AAA where the palette allows).
Do make components tactile: filled navy primary, ambient resting shadow, a real hover lift with the gold border tint.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion with a crossfade or instant fallback for every transition.
donts: Don't build the generic university-CMS faculty homepage: no sidebar nav, stock photography, cramped CV dump, or dated typography.
Don't reach for SaaS/startup landing tropes: no gradient-text headings, no hero-metric template, no identical icon-heading-text card grids, no tracked-uppercase eyebrow above every section.
Don't set Brushed Gold (#c4913c) as body text on light backgrounds; it fails contrast.
Don't add a third type family or break the serif-heading / sans-body split.
Don't let resting shadows get heavy; the drama is in the hover change, not the rest state.
Don't introduce a second saturated accent; gold is the only voice.
